headline: Barry Callebaut launches Flavourcode; Planet A cocoa powder replacer; US dye-ban and UPF pressure
summary: Barry Callebaut launched Flavourcode, a controlled cocoa fermentation platform for consistent chocolate flavour, the most covered story of the week and a direct challenge to Belcolade's own fermentation work.
Planet A Foods (ChoViva) moved into cocoa powder with a high-fibre Cocoa Booster pitched at cocoa costs and GLP-1 users, widening its overlap with Belcolade and patisserie fillings.
Competitors launched bakery texture tools: Roquette a hydrocolloid system for gluten-free bread and Palsgaard a cake emulsifier, both worth benchmarking against Puratos mixes and improvers.
Plant-based egg and dairy replacement scaled up, with Meala tripling pea-protein output and Andfoods launching a fermented black-gram whipped cream.
Regulatory: a federal bill to ban synthetic dyes and growing pressure for a US ultra-processed food definition both point to more reformulation work on glazes, fillings, bread and cakes.
